resources.string: Blocks incognito browsing and adult sites

Looks for incognito / private mode indicators on browser screens and closes those windows. It only reads the screens of the listed browser apps. It does not store the websites you visit and never sends anything off the device.

This app only looks for the “incognito mode” indicator on browser screens.
· It does not store the addresses or contents of pages you visit
· It never sends any data off this device (records stay here)
· It always shows a notification while it is watching
· The adult-site filter changes the Private DNS setting only when you turn it on. From then on, DNS lookups go to the filter you picked

If you install this on someone else’s device, get their consent first. Monitoring someone without consent is illegal in some countries.

Needed to read the incognito indicator on browser screens. Find IncognitoBlocker in the list and switch it on.
From Android 13 on, accessibility access is locked for apps installed outside the store.\nGo to Settings › Apps › IncognitoBlocker › ⋮ (top right) › “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
Required to pause protection or change settings. Choose a number the monitored person does not know.
Makes the app harder to remove. Note that on Android 7 and later the user can still deactivate the admin in Settings and then uninstall.
Chrome posts a persistent notification while incognito tabs are open. With this permission the app still catches sessions it missed on screen.
Stops the manufacturer’s power saving from killing the guard.

Incognito mode is switched off in Chrome and Edge at the OS policy level — the menu entry is gone entirely, so it cannot be worked around.\n\nBrowsers with no such policy (Firefox, Samsung Internet, DuckDuckGo and others) can only be hidden.
Clears every policy and gives up device-owner rights. Restoring it means starting over from scratch.
Why would I need strong mode?

Basic protection detects an incognito window and closes it, so it is briefly open. Strong mode removes incognito mode from Chrome and Edge altogether.

How to set it up (right after a factory reset, before adding any account):
1. Connect this device to a PC over USB
2. Turn on Developer options › USB debugging
3. Run the command below in a terminal on the PC

Every browser marks incognito mode differently, and the markers change with each app update.
Samsung Internet in particular has no public policy for disabling incognito, so screen detection is the only option.

Turn on diagnostic mode, open incognito mode in that browser, then come back here. The IDs and text actually read from that screen will appear in the history below. Add those values to BrowserRules.kt and detection will start working.
Entering the PIN turns incognito blocking off.

\nAn honest note on the limits: basic mode closes an incognito window right after it opens, rather than preventing it. For a complete block, use step 2 (strong mode). And no mode can stop another device or a newly installed browser.
